recall.answer: Exactness costs invertibility and expressivity limits; VAEs win on architecture freedom. The fair test is held-out NLL at matched budgets.

recall.answer: Tweedie single-step test: sharp there but mushy after full sampling proves the sampler (schedule mismatch), not the model.

recall.question: Loss excellent, samples garbage, masks present. Bug and test?
recall.answer: Off-by-one label shift. Test: shift inputs by one, outputs must shift; constant sequences must not give near-zero loss.

recall.question: Attack 'lower pseudo-perplexity proves the better model'.
recall.answer: Pseudo-perplexity sums to 1.0639, not 1.0: not a likelihood. And tokenizations differ: incomparable scales.

recall.answer: Inception never saw X-rays: the features are irrelevant. Fix: domain features plus human ratings.

recall.question: Attack 'one leaderboard number decides the best model'.
recall.answer: Every metric has a blind spot; one number is one blind spot with confidence.

recall.question: KL 0.0003/dim but sharp reconstructions. Diagnose and fix.
recall.answer: Collapse with a memorizing decoder. Fixes: beta > 1 or KL annealing (objective); weaker decoder (architecture).

recall.question: Attack 'the ELBO gap is just an optimization problem'.
recall.answer: The gap has three sources: amortization, family, optimization. Only the third is just optimization.

recall.question: The objective looks great but far-from-data scores are wrong. Cause and fix?
recall.answer: Score matching only sees data; far away the field is extrapolation. Fix: the noise schedule covers space at many scales.

recall.question: Attack 'score matching needs no assumptions'.
recall.answer: The boundary term must vanish (tails), and p must be smooth with full support.

recall.question: Training loss low but paths cross. Cause and fix?
recall.answer: Independent couplings make conditional targets conflict. Fix: OT couplings (straighter paths).

recall.question: Attack 'flow matching removes all diffusion assumptions'.
